questions.question: What is the actual shape of most living cells, despite how they are often represented in textbook diagrams?
options: They are completely flat 2-dimensional structures.
They have a 3-dimensional shape.
They are always perfect 2-dimensional circles.
They exist only as 1-dimensional lines.

questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only structures commonly found in animal cells?
options: Cytoplasm, cell membrane, nucleus, mitochondria
Cell wall, chloroplast, vacuole, nucleus
Cytoplasm, cell wall, nucleus, chloroplast
Cell membrane, cell wall, mitochondria, vacuole

questions.question: What defines a unicellular organism?
options: It consists of a single living cell.
It has no cells at all.
It is made of millions of different cells.
It contains only plant-like tissues.

questions.question: How do cells function in a multicellular organism?
options: Every cell does exactly the same job.
The organism is made of more than one cell, and different cells take on different jobs.
Only one cell does all the work while the other cells remain inactive.
Cells constantly merge to become one single giant cell.

questions.question: In multicellular organisms, what is formed when cells join together to perform specific jobs?
options: Organs
Organisms
Tissues
Organ systems

questions.question: How are organs related to tissues and organ systems in multicellular organisms?
options: An organ is a single cell that controls tissues.
An organ is a group of tissues working together to do a specific job, and organs work together in an organ system.
An organ is made of organ systems working together to form tissues.
An organ is a type of tissue that has no specific job in an organ system.

questions.question: What are the fundamental, living building blocks that make up all organisms?
options: Atoms
Tissues
Organs
Cells

questions.question: Why do we typically need a microscope to observe individual cells?
options: Cells are usually too small to see with the unaided eye.
Cells only exist when light shines on them.
Cells are invisible to all forms of light.
Cells move too fast to be seen by human eyes.

questions.question: Which structures are found in plant cells but not typically in animal cells?
options: Cytoplasm and nucleus
Cell membrane and mitochondria
Cell wall, vacuole, and sometimes chloroplasts
Mitochondria and nucleus

questions.question: What is the main purpose of adding a stain to a specimen when preparing a microscope slide?
options: To kill any harmful bacteria on the slide.
To make it easier to see some parts of the cells.
To glue the cover slip permanently to the slide.
To increase the actual size of the cells.

questions.question: How should observations made from looking through a light microscope be recorded?
options: Using a scientific line drawing
By painting a detailed watercolor picture
By writing a fictional story about the cells
Using a 3D clay model only

questions.question: What is true about specialised cells in animals and plants?
options: They all have identical round shapes and perform the same tasks.
They have shapes, sizes, and structures that are adapted for the jobs they do.
They do not have any nucleus or cytoplasm.
They are only found in unicellular organisms.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of specialised cells?
options: Red blood cells in animals and root hair cells in plants
Any cell that does not have a specific function
Only cells that make up unicellular bacteria
All cells found in non-living matter

questions.question: Which of the following lists represents the life processes that happen in all living organisms?
options: Movement, reproduction, sensitivity, growth, respiration, excretion, nutrition
Photosynthesis, speech, hearing, walking, sleeping, thinking, breathing
Growth, heating, cooling, melting, evaporation, condensation, freezing
Respiration, digestion, circulation, thinking, reading, writing, speaking

questions.question: When is movement considered a sign of life in an organism?
options: When the organism is blown by the wind.
When the organism moves itself to achieve something.
When water currents push the organism along.
When the organism is moved by gravity down a hill.
